A web page as a block result

Source: R/html-page.R
html_page.Rd

html_page() returns an object that draws as a sandboxed iframe. A script block that ends with it shows the page on its card. Give it either html, a page you write, or url, a page that lives elsewhere.

Usage

html_page(
  html = NULL,
  url = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  height = "auto",
  sandbox = NULL,
  max_rows = 1000L
)

Arguments

html

The page, a single string or a character vector of lines.

url

A URL.

data

A data frame, a list or a vector that scripts in an html page read as blockr.data. NULL for none.

height

Height of the frame: a number of pixels or a CSS length such as "400px" or "50vh". "auto" fits an html page to its content; a URL page cannot be measured and defaults to "600px".

sandbox

The iframe's sandbox attribute, a single string. NULL takes the default for the mode.

max_rows

Rows of data passed to the page. More are dropped with a warning. Inf for no limit.

Value

An object of class html_page.

HTML

html goes into the frame as it is. To put values from R into it, build the string in the script, with paste0(), sprintf() or a package such as glue. htmltools::htmlEscape() escapes a value that may hold < or &.

Scripts in the page read data as JSON from blockr.data, an array of row objects for a data frame, or null without data. Missing values are null. Date-times are written in UTC ("2026-01-02T03:04:05Z").

The data travels to the browser with the page, again each time the block re-renders. max_rows limits it.

The page runs in an iframe with sandbox = "allow-scripts": its CSS and JS cannot reach the board. The sandbox does not keep the page from sending its data to other hosts. A script, an image or a style sheet in the page can load from anywhere and pass along what the page holds. With height = "auto" the iframe grows to fit the page, up to 20000 pixels.

URL

The URL has to start with http:// or https://. A value from R goes in with paste0(); utils::URLencode() with reserved = TRUE encodes it. The other site has to allow framing: a site that sends X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN, or a CSP frame-ancestors that does not list the board's host, stays blank. A link above the frame opens the page in a new tab.

The frame keeps allow-same-origin, because an external app needs its own cookies and storage. The sandbox therefore only protects the board from pages on another host. A URL on the board's own host can reach the board and everything the viewer can do on it.

Outside a board

At the console, printing the object opens the page in the viewer. In a script run with Rscript it prints one line. In an R Markdown or Quarto document with HTML output the frame is part of the document.

Examples

title <- "Hello"
html_page(paste0("<h1>", title, "</h1>"))
#> <html_page> html, 671 characters, height auto

bands <- data.frame(name = c("Mick", "John"), band = c("Stones", "Beatles"))
html_page(
  paste0(
    "<ul>",
    paste0("<li>", bands$name, ": ", bands$band, "</li>", collapse = ""),
    "</ul>"
  )
)
#> <html_page> html, 709 characters, height auto

html_page(
  "<ul id='l'></ul><script>
  blockr.data.forEach(function (r) {
    document.getElementById('l').insertAdjacentHTML(
      'beforeend', '<li>' + r.name + '</li>'
    );
  });
  </script>",
  data = bands
)
#> <html_page> html, 903 characters, height auto

q <- "blockr"
html_page(
  url = paste0("https://example.org/search?q=", utils::URLencode(q, TRUE))
)
#> <html_page> https://example.org/search?q=blockr, height 600px
